title.zh: 卷二十三 志第四: 五行
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第四: 五行 Volume 23 Treatises 4: Five Elements

sentences.zh: 五行之精氣，在天為五緯，在地為五材，在人為五常及五事。

translations.literal: The quintessential qi of the Five Elements—in Heaven are the five planets, on Earth the five materials, in humanity the Five Constants and the Five Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The refined qi of the Five Elements becomes the five planets in Heaven, the five materials on Earth, and in humanity the Five Constants and the Five Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五緯志諸《天文》，歷代皆然。

translations.literal: Records of the five planets belong in the Astronomy treatises, as in every dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets are recorded in the Astronomy treatises, as every dynasty has done.

sentences.zh: 其形質在地，性情在人，休咎各以其類，為感應於兩間者，歷代又有《五行志》焉。

translations.literal: Their form and substance lie on Earth, their disposition in humanity; auspicious and inauspicious signs each follow their kind—as responses between the two realms—dynasties have also compiled Treatises on the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: Form and substance belong to Earth, disposition to humanity; auspicious and inauspicious signs each keep to their kind—as resonances between the two realms—and dynasties have also compiled Treatises on the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 兩漢以來，儒者若夏侯勝之徒，專以《洪範五行》為學，作史者多采其說，凡言某征之休咎，則以某事之得失系之，而配之以五行。

translations.literal: Since the Two Han, scholars such as Xia Hou Sheng made the Hong Fan's Five Elements their sole study; historians mostly adopted their views—whenever they spoke of the auspicious or inauspicious bearing of some omen, they tied it to the success or failure of some affair and matched it to the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Two Han, scholars such as Xia Hou Sheng took the Hong Fan's Five Elements as their whole craft; historians mostly followed them—whenever they judged an omen auspicious or inauspicious, they bound it to some affair's success or failure and paired it with the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 謂其盡然，其弊不免于傅會；

translations.literal: To hold this wholly true cannot escape the fault of forced correlation;
translations.idiomatic: To hold this wholly true cannot escape the fault of forced correlation;

sentences.zh: 謂其不然，「肅，時雨若」、「蒙，恆風若」之類，箕子蓋嘗言之。

translations.literal: to hold it wholly false—sayings such as "With respect, seasonable rain follows" and "With obscurity, constant wind follows"—Jizi surely spoke them.
translations.idiomatic: to hold it wholly false—sayings such as "With respect, seasonable rain follows" and "With obscurity, constant wind follows"—Jizi surely spoke them.

sentences.zh: 金世未能一天下，天文災祥猶有星野之說，五行休咎見於國內者不得他諉，乃匯其史氏所書，仍前史法，作《五行志》。

translations.literal: The Jin age could not unite all under Heaven; celestial disaster and blessing still spoke of astrological fields, but Five Elements omens appearing within the realm could not be blamed elsewhere—so they gathered what their historians wrote, following earlier annalistic form, and composed this Treatise on the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin age had not united the realm; celestial disaster and blessing still invoked the doctrine of stellar fields, yet Five Elements omens seen within their borders could not be blamed on others—so they gathered what their historians recorded, following earlier annalistic form, and composed this Treatise on the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 至於五常五事之感應，則不必泥漢儒為例雲。

translations.literal: As for responses of the Five Constants and Five Affairs, there is no need to bind oneself to Han Confucian precedent.
translations.idiomatic: As for responses of the Five Constants and Five Affairs, there is no need to bind oneself to Han Confucian precedent.

sentences.zh: 初，金之興，平定諸部，屢有禎異，故世祖每與敵戰，嘗以夢寐卜其勝負。

translations.literal: At the Jin rise, pacifying the tribes, miraculous signs recurred again and again—hence the Shizu Emperor, whenever he fought enemies, would read victory or defeat in his dreams.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first rose and pacified the tribes, portents came again and again—so Shizu, whenever he met the enemy in battle, would read victory or defeat in his dreams.

sentences.zh: 烏春兵至蘇東海甸，世祖曰：「予夙昔有異夢，不可親戰，若左軍有力戰者當克。

translations.literal: When Wuchun's army reached the Suhai pasturelands, Shizu said: "I had an uncanny dream of old—I must not fight in person; if someone on the left wing fights with full force, we shall win.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchun's army reached the Suhai pasturelands, Shizu said: "Long ago I had an uncanny dream—I must not fight in person; if someone on the left wing fights with all his strength, we shall win.

sentences.zh: 」既而與肅宗等擊之，敵大敗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Suzong and others struck them, and the enemy was routed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he and Suzong and others struck them, and the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 太祖之生也，常有五色雲氣若二千斛廩囷之狀，屢見東方。

translations.literal: At the Founder Ancestor's birth, five-colored cloud-qi often shaped like a two-thousand-bushel granary-bin was seen again and again in the east.
translations.idiomatic: At the Founder Ancestor's birth, five-colored cloud-qi often shaped like a two-thousand-bushel granary-bin was seen again and again in the east.

sentences.zh: 遼司天到孔致和曰：「其下當生異人，建非常之事，天以象告，非人力所能為也。」

translations.literal: Liao Director of Astronomy Dao Kong Zhihe said: "Beneath it an extraordinary man shall be born, to accomplish unheard-of deeds—Heaven announces by signs what human effort cannot bring about."
translations.idiomatic: Liao Director of Astronomy Dao Kong Zhihe said: "Beneath it an extraordinary man shall be born, to accomplish unheard-of deeds—Heaven announces by signs what no human hand can make."

sentences.zh: 溫都部跋忒畔，穆宗遣太祖討之，入辭，奏曰：「昨夕見赤祥，往必克。

translations.literal: When the Wendu tribal chief Bate rebelled, Muzong sent the Founder Ancestor to subdue him; on taking leave he reported: "Last night I saw a crimson auspice—we shall win when we go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wendu tribal chief Bate rebelled, Muzong sent the Founder Ancestor to subdue him; on taking leave he reported: "Last night I saw a crimson auspice—we shall win when we go.

sentences.zh: 」遂與跋忒戰，殺之。

translations.literal: " He fought Bate and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " He fought Bate and killed him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗攻阿疏日，辰巳間，忽暴雨昏曀，雷電環阿疏所居，是夕有巨火聲如雷，墜阿疏城中，遂攻下之。

translations.literal: When Muzong besieged Ashuri, between the chen and si hours a violent rainstorm darkened the sky; lightning ringed Ashuri's dwelling; that night a great fire, thunder-loud, fell into Ashuri's town—and the place was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong besieged Ashuri, between the chen and si hours a violent rainstorm darkened the sky; lightning ringed Ashuri's dwelling; that night a great fire, loud as thunder, fell into Ashuri's town—and the place was taken.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗往甯江，夢斡帶之禾場焚，頃刻而盡。

translations.literal: The Founder Ancestor once went to Ningjiang and dreamed that Wandai's threshing-floor burned to nothing in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder Ancestor once went to Ningjiang and dreamed that Wandai's threshing-floor burned to nothing in an instant.

sentences.zh: 覺而大戚，即馳還，斡帶已寢疾，翌日不起。

translations.literal: Waking, he grieved deeply and galloped back—Wandai had already taken to his bed, and the next day would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Waking, he grieved deeply and galloped back—Wandai had already taken to his bed, and the next day would not rise.

sentences.zh: 斡塞伐高麗，太祖臥而得夢，及起曰：「今日捷音必至。

translations.literal: When Wosai campaigned against Goryeo, the Founder Ancestor slept and dreamed; on rising he said: "Today the news of victory must arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When Wosai campaigned against Goryeo, the Founder Ancestor slept and dreamed; on rising he said: "Today the news of victory must arrive.

sentences.zh: 」乃為具於球場以待。

translations.literal: " He had a feast laid on the ball-court to await it.
translations.idiomatic: " He had a feast laid on the ball-court to await it.

sentences.zh: 有二麞渡水而至，獲之，太祖曰：「此休征也。

translations.literal: Two roe deer crossed the water and were taken; the Founder Ancestor said: "This is an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: Two roe deer crossed the water and were taken; the Founder Ancestor said: "This is an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 」言未既，捷書至，眾大異之。

translations.literal: " The words were barely spoken when the victory dispatch arrived—the crowd marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " He had scarcely finished when the victory dispatch arrived—and the whole camp stood amazed.

sentences.zh: 他日軍甯江，駐高阜，撒改仰見太祖體如喬松，所乘馬如岡阜之大，太祖亦視撒改人馬異常，撒改因白所見，太祖喜曰：「此吉兆也。

translations.literal: Another day, campaigning at Ningjiang, they halted on a high mound; Sacai looking up saw the Founder Ancestor's body like a towering pine, his mount like a hill-crest in scale; the Founder Ancestor also saw Sacai's horse and men extraordinary. Sacai told what he had seen; the Founder Ancestor rejoiced: "This is a lucky sign.
translations.idiomatic: Another day, campaigning at Ningjiang, they halted on a high mound; Sacai looking up saw the Founder Ancestor's body like a towering pine, his mount like a hill-crest in scale; the Founder Ancestor also saw Sacai's horse and men extraordinary. Sacai told what he had seen; the Founder Ancestor rejoiced: "This is a lucky sign.

sentences.zh: 」即舉酒酹之曰：「異日成功，當識此地。

translations.literal: " He raised wine and libated, saying: "When we succeed another day, remember this place.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised wine and libated, saying: "When we succeed another day, remember this place.

sentences.zh: 」師次唐括帶斡甲之地，諸軍介而立，有光起於人足及戈矛上，明日，至劄只水，光復如初。

translations.literal: " The army halted at Tangkuodaiwogan; the troops stood arrayed, and light rose from men's feet and from spear-points; the next day, reaching Zhazhi River, the light appeared as before.
translations.idiomatic: " The army halted at Tangkuodaiwogan; the troops stood arrayed, and light rose from men's feet and from spear-points; the next day, reaching Zhazhi River, the light appeared as before.

sentences.zh: 收國元年，上在甯江州，有光正圓，自空而墜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shouguo, the sovereign was at Ningjiang; a perfectly round light fell from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shouguo, the sovereign was at Ningjiang; a perfectly round light fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 八月己卯，黃龍見空中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jimao, a yellow dragon appeared in the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jimao, a yellow dragon appeared in the sky.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁未，上候遼軍還至熟結濼，有光復見於矛端。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, dingwei, the sovereign waited for Liao forces, returning to Shujie Marsh—and the light was seen again on spear-tips.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, dingwei, the sovereign waited for Liao forces, returning to Shujie Marsh—and the light was seen again on spear-tips.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年三月，師攻西京，有火如鬥，墜其城中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, third month, the army besieged Western Capital; a fire the size of a dipper-measure fell into its walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu, third month, the army besieged Western Capital; a fire the size of a dipper-measure fell into its walls.

sentences.zh: 是月，城降而複叛，四月辛卯，取之。

translations.literal: That month the city surrendered then rebelled again; in the fourth month, xinmao, it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: That month the city surrendered then rebelled again; in the fourth month, xinmao, it was taken.

sentences.zh: 太宗天會二年，曷懶移鹿古水霖雨害稼，且為蝗所食。

translations.literal: Taizong, second year of Tianhui, at Yilanyilugu River—incessant rain harmed the crops, and locusts devoured them besides.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, second year of Tianhui, at Yilanyilugu River—incessant rain harmed the crops, and locusts devoured them besides.

sentences.zh: 秋，泰州潦，害稼。

translations.literal: In autumn, Taizhou flooded, ruining the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Taizhou flooded, ruining the harvest.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，錦州野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Third year, seventh month—at Jinzhou wild silkworms formed cocoons.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, seventh month—at Jinzhou wild silkworms formed cocoons.

sentences.zh: 九月，廣寧府進嘉禾。

translations.literal: Ninth month—Guangning Prefecture presented auspicious grain.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month—Guangning Prefecture presented auspicious grain.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，中京進嘉禾。

translations.literal: Fourth year, tenth month—Central Capital presented auspicious grain.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, tenth month—Central Capital presented auspicious grain.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，移懶路饑。

translations.literal: Sixth year, winter—Yilan circuit suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, winter—Yilan circuit suffered famine.

sentences.zh: 九年七月丙申，上禦西樓聽政，聞咸州所貢白鵲音忽異常，上起視之，見東樓上光明中有像巍然高五丈許，下有紅雲承之，若世所謂佛者，乃擎跽修虔，久之而沒。

translations.literal: Ninth year, seventh month, bingshen—the sovereign held court on the west tower and heard the white magpie presented from Xianzhou cry oddly; he rose to look and saw on the east tower, within a blaze of light, a figure towering some five zhang, red cloud beneath bearing it up like the Buddha the world knows—he raised his joined hands in reverence until it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, seventh month, bingshen—the sovereign held court on the west tower and heard the white magpie presented from Xianzhou cry oddly; he rose to look and saw on the east tower, within a blaze of light, a figure towering some five zhang, red cloud beneath bearing it up like the Buddha the world knows—he raised his joined hands in reverence until it vanished.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，移懶、曷懶等路饑。

translations.literal: Tenth year, winter—Yilan, Yilanyilugu, and other circuits starved.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year, winter—Yilan, Yilanyilugu, and other circuits starved.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天會十三年五月，甘露降于盧州熊嶽縣。

translations.literal: Xizong, thirteenth year of Tianhui, fifth month—sweet dew fell in Xiongyue County, Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong, thirteenth year of Tianhui, fifth month—sweet dew fell in Xiongyue County, Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月辛巳，有司進四足雀。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year, seventh month, xinsi—the authorities presented a four-footed sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth year, seventh month, xinsi—the authorities presented a four-footed sparrow.

sentences.zh: 丙戌夜，京師地震。

translations.literal: On the night of bingxu the capital shook in earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingxu the capital shook in earthquake.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年夏，有龍見於熙州野水，凡三日。

translations.literal: First year of Tianjuan, summer—a dragon was seen in the wild waters of Xizhou, for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: First year of Tianjuan, summer—a dragon was seen in the wild waters of Xizhou, for three days in all.

sentences.zh: 初，于水面見一蒼龍，良久而沒。

translations.literal: At first an azure dragon showed on the water's face and, after a long while, sank away.
translations.idiomatic: At first an azure dragon showed on the water's face and, after a long while, sank away.

sentences.zh: 次日，見金龍一，爪承一嬰兒，兒為龍所戲，略無懼色，三日如故。

translations.literal: The next day a golden dragon appeared, its claw bearing an infant the dragon sported with—the child showing no fear—for three days unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a golden dragon appeared, its claw bearing an infant the dragon sported with—the child showing no fear—for three days unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又見一人，乘白馬，紅袍玉帶，如少年官狀，馬前有六蟾蜍，凡三時乃沒，郡人競往觀之。

translations.literal: Again a man was seen, riding a white horse in red robe and jade belt like a youthful officer, six toads before his horse; after three watch-periods all vanished, and the county folk rushed to see.
translations.idiomatic: Again a man was seen, riding a white horse in red robe and jade belt like a youthful officer, six toads before his horse; after three watch-periods all vanished, and the county folk rushed to see.

sentences.zh: 七月丁酉，按出滸河溢，壞民廬舍。

translations.literal: Seventh month, dingyou—the Anchu River burst its banks, wrecking commoners' homes.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, dingyou—the Anchu River burst its banks, wrecking commoners' homes.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月丁丑，地震。

translations.literal: Third year, twelfth month, dingchou—earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, twelfth month, dingchou—earthquake.

sentences.zh: 海陵天德二年十二月，野人采石炭，獲異香。

translations.literal: Hailing, twelfth month of the second year of Tiande—a countryman mining coal found a strange fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, twelfth month of the second year of Tiande—a countryman mining coal found a strange fragrance.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年五月癸丑，南京大內災。

translations.literal: Third year of Zhenyuan, fifth month, guichou—fire disaster in the Nanjing inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Zhenyuan, fifth month, guichou—fire disaster in the Nanjing inner palace.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月己丑，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jichou—rain, and trees armored in ice.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jichou—it rained, and the trees were sheathed in ice.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年六月壬辰，蝗飛入京師。

translations.literal: Zhenglong, second year, sixth month, on renchen: locusts flew into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong, second year, sixth month, on renchen: locusts flew into the capital.

sentences.zh: 秋，中都、山東、河東蝗。

translations.literal: Autumn: locusts in the Central Capital, Shandong, and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn locusts struck the Central Capital, Shandong, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月庚寅，霜附木。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, on gengyin: frost clung to trees.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, eleventh month, on gengyin: frost clung to the trees.

sentences.zh: 五年二月辛未，河東、陝西地震。

translations.literal: Fifth year, second month, on xinwei: earthquakes in Hedong and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, second month, on xinwei: earthquakes in Hedong and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮戎、德順等軍大風，壞廬舍，民多壓死。

translations.literal: At Zhenrong, Deshun, and other armies a great wind destroyed dwellings; many people were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenrong, Deshun, and other armies a great wind destroyed dwellings and crushed many people to death.

sentences.zh: 海陵問司天馬貴中等曰：「何為地震？

translations.literal: Hailing asked Ma Guizhong of the Directorate of Astronomy and others, saying: 「What causes an earthquake?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked Ma Guizhong of the Directorate of Astronomy and others: 「What causes an earthquake?

sentences.zh: 」貴中等曰：「伏陽逼陰所致。

translations.literal: 」Ma Guizhong and the others said: 「It comes of submerged yang pressing yin.
translations.idiomatic: 」Ma Guizhong and the others said: 「Submerged yang pressing yin causes it.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「震而大風，何也？

translations.literal: 」He asked again: 「When there is earthquake and great wind, what of it?
translations.idiomatic: 」He asked again: 「When earthquake comes with great wind, what does that mean?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「土失其性，則地以震。

translations.literal: 」They replied: 「When earth loses its proper nature, the ground quakes.
translations.idiomatic: 」They replied: 「When earth loses its proper nature, the ground quakes.

sentences.zh: 風為號令，人君嚴急則有風及物之災。

translations.literal: Wind is command; when the ruler is harsh and urgent there are winds and disasters reaching things.
translations.idiomatic: Wind is command; when the ruler is harsh and urgent, wind disasters reach things as well.

sentences.zh: 」六年六月壬戌，大風壞承天門鴟尾。

translations.literal: 」Sixth year, sixth month, on renxu: a great wind destroyed the owl-tail ridge ornaments of Chengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: 」Sixth year, sixth month, on renxu: a great wind destroyed the owl-tail ridge ornaments of Chengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世宗居貞懿皇后憂，在遼陽，一日方寢，有紅光照其室，及其龍見於室上，又夜有大星流入其邸。

translations.literal: That year Shizong was in mourning for Empress Zhenyi at Liaoyang; one day as he slept a red light filled his chamber, and a dragon appeared above the room; by night a great star streamed into his residence.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shizong was mourning Empress Zhenyi at Liaoyang; one day as he slept a red light filled his chamber, a dragon appeared above the room, and by night a great star streamed into his residence.

sentences.zh: 八月，複有雲氣自西來，黃龍見其中，人皆見之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month cloud-vapor came again from the west, and a yellow dragon appeared within it; everyone saw it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month cloud-vapor came again from the west with a yellow dragon within it; everyone saw it.

sentences.zh: 是時，臨潢府聞空中有車馬聲，仰視見風雲杳靄，神鬼兵甲蔽天，自北而南，仍有語促行者。

translations.literal: At that time Linhuang Prefecture heard the sound of chariots and horses in the sky; looking up they saw wind and cloud misty and dim, spirits and ghosts with armor filling heaven from north to south, and still voices urging travelers on.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Linhuang Prefecture heard chariots and horses in the sky; looking up they saw misty wind and cloud, spirit soldiers in armor filling the sky from north to south, and voices urging travelers on.

sentences.zh: 未歲，海陵下詔南征。

translations.literal: Before the year was out, Hailing issued an edict for the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year was out, Hailing issued an edict for the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定二年閏二月辛卯，神龍殿十六位焚，延及太和、厚德殿。

translations.literal: Shizong, Dading second year, intercalary second month, on xinmao: the sixteen spirit-tablets of Shendian Hall burned, spreading to Taihe and Houde halls.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, Dading second year, intercalary second month, on xinmao: the sixteen spirit-tablets of Shendian Hall burned and the fire spread to Taihe and Houde halls.

sentences.zh: 三年三月丙申，中都以南八路蝗。

translations.literal: Third year, third month, on bingshen: locusts in the Eight Routes south of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, third month, on bingshen: locusts in the Eight Routes south of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 四年三月庚子夜，京師地震。

translations.literal: Fourth year, third month, on gengzi night: earthquake in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, third month, on gengzi at night: the capital was shaken by earthquake.

sentences.zh: 七年辛丑，大風雷雨，拔木。

translations.literal: Seventh year, xinchou: great wind, thunder, and rain; trees were uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, xinchou: great wind, thunder, and rain uprooted trees.

translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: drought.

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, first month, the Ministry of the Masters of Writing memorialized: 「Zhang Xiaoshan of Wanping had a son named Hede; on the morning of the third month of Dading twelfth year he died of illness, but at dusk revived, saying he was Xi'er, son of Wang Jian of Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 而喜兒前三年已死，建驗以家事，能具道之。

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「若是則奸幸小人競生詐偽，瀆亂人倫。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, eighth month, new moon on dingsi, halting at Cifali She: at noon a white dragon appeared in a small creek east of the imperial tent; it then rode up on thunder-clouds, its tail still trailing the ground, and after long went north.

translations.idiomatic: That year drought and locusts afflicted the Central Capital, Hebei, Shandong, Shaanxi, Hedong, Liaodong, and the like among ten circuits.

translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year, seventh month: great rain; the Hutuo and Lugou rivers overflowed and the Yellow River broke at Baigou.

translations.literal: Twentieth year, fourth month, on jihai: fire at the gate of Taining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Twentieth year, fourth month, on jihai: fire at the gate of Taining Palace.

translations.literal: Fifth month, bingyin: the capital earthquake; black and white hair grew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingyin, the capital was shaken by an earthquake and black and white hair sprouted from the ground.

sentences.zh: 七月，旱。

translations.literal: Seventh month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 秋，河決衛州。

translations.literal: Autumn: the Yellow River broke its banks at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the Yellow River burst its banks at Weizhou.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, fifth month, locust nymphs appeared at Qingdu and spread over more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 一夕大風，蝗皆不見。

translations.literal: One night a great wind blew and the locusts all vanished.
translations.idiomatic: One night a great wind rose and every locust disappeared.

translations.literal: Fifth month, dinghai: hail fell and white hair grew from the ground.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, first month, on the xinmao new moon, Xuzhou presented eighteen stalks of lingzhi.

translations.idiomatic: At Zhending two stalks of auspicious grain grew, in separate fields yet sharing one ear.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, fourth month, on xinchou, the capital was lightly shaken.

translations.idiomatic: Hejian Prefecture presented auspicious grain.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，御史中丞董師中奏：「乃者太白晝見，京師地震，北方有赤氣，遲明始散。

translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, third month, Vice Censor-in-Chief Dong Shizhong memorialized: "Lately Venus has shown in daytime, the capital has been shaken by earthquake, and red vapor in the north lingered until dawn was far advanced.

sentences.zh: 天之示象，冀有以警悟聖主也。

translations.literal: Heaven’s display of signs is meant, I trust, to awaken the sage ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s signs are meant, I trust, to awaken the sage ruler."

sentences.zh: 」上問：「所言天象何從得之？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked: "From whom did you learn these celestial signs?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "How did you learn of these celestial signs?"

sentences.zh: 」師中曰：「前監察御史陳元升得之于一司天長行。

translations.literal: " Shizhong said: "Former Investigating Censor Chen Yuansheng learned them from a senior clerk of the Directorate of Astronomy."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizhong said, "Former Investigating Censor Chen Yuansheng heard them from a senior clerk of the Directorate of Astronomy."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「司天臺官不奏固有罪，其以語人尤非。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Directorate of Astronomy officials are surely guilty for not reporting, but telling others is especially wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Directorate officials are surely guilty for not reporting, but spreading word to others is especially wrong.

sentences.zh: 朕欲令自今司天有事而不奏者長行得言之，何如？

translations.literal: I wish that hereafter when the Directorate has a matter and does not report it, senior clerks may speak of it—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish that hereafter when the Directorate has a matter and does not report it, senior clerks may speak up—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」師中曰：「善。

translations.literal: " Shizhong said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizhong said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」五月，霖雨，命有司祈晴。

translations.literal: " Fifth month: prolonged rain; officials were ordered to pray for clear weather.

translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Yellow River burst at Weizhou and Wei, Qing, and Cang were all harmed.

translations.idiomatic: That year Hebei, Shandong, Nanjing, and Shaanxi circuits all enjoyed a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 邢、洺、深、冀及河北西路十六謀克之地，野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: In the sixteen meng’an districts of Xing, Ming, Shen, Ji, and the Hebei West Circuit, wild silkworms formed cocoons.
translations.idiomatic: Across the sixteen meng’an districts of Xing, Ming, Shen, Ji, and Hebei West Circuit, wild silkworms spun cocoons.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬午，木冰。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, renwu: tree glaze.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renwu, trees were coated with glaze ice.

translations.literal: Fifth year, seventh month, bingxu: the Heavenly Longevity Festival; rain and overcast had continued for days, but on this day the sky cleared, and a dragon trailed its tail through the clouds before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, seventh month, on bingxu, the Heavenly Longevity Festival: rain and cloud had lasted for days, but that day the sky cleared and a dragon dragged its tail through the clouds before the hall.

sentences.zh: 八月，河決陽武故堤，灌封丘而東。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Yellow River broke the old embankment at Yangwu and flooded east past Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Yellow River breached the old embankment at Yangwu and poured east past Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁丑，京師地震，大雨雹，晝晦，大風，震應天門左鴟尾壞。

translations.literal: Sixth year, second month, dingchou: the capital was shaken by earthquake; great hail fell; the day was darkened; a great wind blew and the owl-tail ornament on the left of the Gate of Responding to Heaven was broken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, second month, on dingchou, the capital was shaken by earthquake; great hail fell; daylight was dimmed; a great wind blew and broke the left owl-tail ornament on the Gate of Responding to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，大雨震電，有龍起於渾儀鰲趺，台忽中裂而摧。

translations.literal: Sixth year, eighth month: great rain, thunder, and lightning; a dragon rose from the tortoise pedestal of the armillary sphere; the terrace suddenly split down the middle and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, eighth month, heavy rain, thunder, and lightning struck; a dragon rose from the tortoise pedestal of the armillary sphere; the terrace suddenly split and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 儀僕於台下。

translations.literal: The instrument fell below the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The instrument fell beneath the terrace.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年八月丙申，磁州武安縣鼓山石聖台，有大鳥十集於臺上，其羽五色爛然，文多赤黃，赭冠雞項，尾闊而修，狀若鯉魚尾而長，高可逾人，九子差小侍傍，亦高四五尺。

translations.literal: Taihe second year, eighth month, bingshen: at the Stone Drum Mountain Sage Terrace in Wu’an County, Cizhou, ten great birds gathered on the terrace; their feathers were brilliantly five-colored, mostly red and yellow; ochre crest and chicken neck; tail broad and long, shaped like a carp’s tail and tall enough to surpass a man; nine young somewhat smaller attended at the side, likewise four or five chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe, eighth month, on bingshen, at the Stone Drum Mountain Sage Terrace in Wu’an County, Cizhou, ten great birds gathered on the terrace; their feathers shone in five colors, mostly red and yellow; ochre crest and chicken neck; tail broad and long like a carp’s tail and taller than a man; nine smaller young stood beside them, each four or five chi high.

sentences.zh: 禽鳥萬數形色各異，或飛或蹲，或步或立，皆成行列，首皆正向如朝拱然。

translations.literal: Myriad birds of every shape and color either flew or crouched, walked or stood, all in ranks with their heads turned forward as if bowing in court.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad birds of every shape and color flew or crouched, walked or stood, all in ranks facing forward as if bowing in court.

sentences.zh: 初自東南來，勢如連雲，聲如殷雷，林木震動，牧者驚惶，即驅牛擊物以驚之，殊不為動。

translations.literal: At first they came from the southeast like linked clouds, sounding like rolling thunder; trees shook; herdsmen were terrified and drove cattle and struck objects to scare them, yet they did not stir at all.
translations.idiomatic: At first they came from the southeast like linked clouds, roaring like thunder; trees shook; herdsmen panicked and drove cattle and struck things to scare them, yet the birds did not stir.

sentences.zh: 俄有大鳥如雕鶚者怒來搏擊之，民益恐，奔告縣官，皆以為鳳凰也，命工圖上之。

translations.literal: Soon a great bird like an eagle came angrily to strike them; the people grew more afraid and ran to tell the county officials, who all took them for phoenixes and ordered artisans to paint them and submit the pictures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a great bird like an eagle came furiously to strike them; the people grew more afraid and reported to the county, where all called them phoenixes and ordered artisans to paint them and submit the pictures.

sentences.zh: 留二日西北去。

translations.literal: After two days they went off to the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: After two days they departed to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 按視其處，糞跡數頃，其色各異。

translations.literal: On inspecting the place, droppings covered several qing, each of a different color.
translations.idiomatic: On inspecting the site, droppings covered several qing, each of a different color.

sentences.zh: 遺禽數千，累日不能去。

translations.literal: Thousands of birds remained behind; for many days they would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of birds lingered and would not depart for many days.

sentences.zh: 所食皆巨鯉，大者丈餘，魚骨蔽地。

translations.literal: What they ate were all giant carp; the largest were more than ten chi; fish bones covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: They fed on giant carp, some more than ten chi long, until fish bones carpeted the ground.

sentences.zh: 章宗以其事告宗廟，詔中外。

translations.literal: Zhangzong reported the matter to the ancestral temple and issued an edict to the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong reported the affair to the ancestral temple and proclaimed it throughout court and realm.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，旱。

translations.literal: Year 3, fourth month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, fourth month, there was drought.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，大風。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on jihai: a great wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jihai, a great wind rose.

sentences.zh: 四年正月壬申，陰霧，木冰。

translations.literal: Year 4, first month, on renshen: overcast gloom; tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, first month, on renshen, gloom hung low and tree ice formed.

sentences.zh: 三月丁卯，大風，毀宣陽門鴟尾。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingmao: a great wind destroyed the owl-tail finial of Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao, a great wind broke the owl-tail finial of Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 四月，旱。

translations.literal: Fourth month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，萬甯宮端門災。

translations.literal: On renxu the main gate of Wanning Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu fire struck the main gate of Wanning Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁卯，陰。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on dingmao: overcast.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, the sky stayed overcast.

sentences.zh: 木冰凡三日。

translations.literal: Tree ice lasted three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Tree ice lasted three days altogether.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，旱。

translations.literal: Fifth year, summer: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, summer brought drought.

sentences.zh: 八年閏四月甲午，雨雹。

translations.literal: Eighth year, intercalary fourth month, on jiawu: hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, intercalary fourth month, on jiawu, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 河南路蝗。

translations.literal: Henan Circuit had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts appeared in Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，飛蝗入京畿。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on wuzi: flying locusts entered the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi, flying locusts entered the capital region.

sentences.zh: 八月乙酉，有虎至陽春門外，駕出射獲之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on yiyou: a tiger came to the outside of Yangchun Gate; the emperor went out and shot and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiyou, a tiger reached the outside of Yangchun Gate; the emperor went out, shot it, and killed it.

sentences.zh: 時又有童謠雲：「易水流，汴水流，更年易過又休休。

translations.literal: At the time there was also a children's ballad that said: 「The Yishui flows, the Bian River flows; years pass easily and all is at rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a children's ballad ran: 「The Yishui flows, the Bian flows; the years turn easily and all grows still.

sentences.zh: 兩家都好住，前後總成留。

translations.literal: Both households may dwell well; before and after all becomes liu.」
translations.idiomatic: Both homes may settle well; before and after all comes to stay.」

sentences.zh: 」至貞*中，舉國遷汴。

translations.literal: By the Zhenyou era the whole state moved to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyou era the entire realm relocated to Bian.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王大安元年，徐、邳界黃河清五百餘裏，幾二年，以其事詔中外。

translations.literal: Shao Wang, Da'an year 1: along the Xu and Pi border the Yellow River ran clear for more than five hundred li, nearly two years; an edict on the matter was sent to court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Shao Wang's first Da'an year the Yellow River ran clear along the Xu–Pi border for more than five hundred li for nearly two years, and an edict proclaimed it throughout court and realm.

sentences.zh: 臨洮人楊珪上書曰：「河性本濁，而今反清，是水失其性也。

translations.literal: Yang Gui of Lintao submitted a memorial saying: 「The river's nature is turbid, yet now it has turned clear — the water has lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui of Lintao memorialized: 「The Yellow River is naturally muddy; that it has turned clear means the water has lost its true nature.

sentences.zh: 正猶天動地靜，使當動者靜，當靜者動，則如之何，其為災異明矣。

translations.literal: It is just as when heaven should move and earth should be still — if what should move is made still and what should be still is made to move, what then can be done? The thing is plainly a portent of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: It is like heaven stirring and earth resting: if what must move is stilled and what must rest is stirred, how can order hold? The omen of calamity is plain.

sentences.zh: 且《傳》曰：'黃河青，聖人生。

translations.literal: Moreover the Tradition says: 「When the Yellow River turns green, a sage is born.」
translations.idiomatic: Moreover tradition says: 「When the Yellow River turns green, a sage is born.」

sentences.zh: '假使聖人生，恐不在今日。

translations.literal: Even if a sage were born, he is unlikely to appear in our day.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a sage were born, he would hardly appear in our own time.

sentences.zh: 又曰'黃河清，諸侯為天子。

translations.literal: It also says: 「When the Yellow River clears, feudal lords become Son of Heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 「When the Yellow River clears, lords become Son of Heaven.」

sentences.zh: '正當戒懼，以銷災變，而複誇示四方，臣所未喻。

translations.literal: One ought rather to be vigilant and dispel the omen, yet instead it is displayed to the four quarters — this your subject cannot understand.」
translations.idiomatic: The court ought to be wary and dispel the portent, not boast of it to the four quarters — a point your subject cannot fathom.」

sentences.zh: 」宰相以為妖言，議誅之，慮絕言路，即詔大興鎖銷還本管。

translations.literal: The chancellors deemed it demon talk and discussed putting him to death, but fearing to cut off the path of remonstrance they instead edicted Daxing to lock and escort him back to his native circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors called it demonic speech and debated execution, yet fearing to choke off remonstrance they edicted Daxing to detain him in irons and return him to his home circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙申，平陽地震，有聲自西北來。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on bingshen: Pingyang earthquake; a sound came from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen, Pingyang quaked and a rumble rolled in from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 戊戌夜，又震，自此時複震動，浮山縣尤劇，城廨民居圮者十七八，死者凡二三千人。

translations.literal: On wuxu night it shook again; from then on tremors recurred, worst in Fushan county — seventeen or eighteen out of ten city offices and private dwellings collapsed, and the dead numbered two or three thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu night it shook again, and tremors kept returning, worst in Fushan county: seven or eight dwellings in ten were ruined, and two or three thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 二年二月乙酉，地大震，有聲殷殷然。

translations.literal: Year 2, second month, on yiyou: a great earthquake; the sound was deep and rolling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, second month, on yiyou, a great earthquake rumbled deep and long.

sentences.zh: 六月、七月至九月晦。

translations.literal: From the sixth and seventh months until the end of the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth and seventh months until the ninth month's last day.

sentences.zh: 其震不一。

translations.literal: The shocks were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The tremors did not come alike.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京師民周修武宅前渠內火出，高二尺，焚其板橋。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: before the house of the capital resident Zhou Xiuwu, fire burst from the canal ditch two chi high and burned his plank bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month fire erupted from the canal ditch before Zhou Xiuwu's house in the capital, rose two chi, and burned his plank bridge.

sentences.zh: 又旬日，大悲閣幡竿下石隙中火出，高二三尺，人近之即滅，凡十餘日。

translations.literal: Ten days later fire burst from a stone crevice beneath the banner pole at Great Compassion Pavilion, two or three chi high; when people drew near it went out — this lasted more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later fire shot from a stone crack under the banner pole at Great Compassion Pavilion, two or three chi high; anyone who neared it saw the flame die — for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 自是都城連夜燔爇二三十處。

translations.literal: From then on the capital burned in twenty or thirty places every night.
translations.idiomatic: After that the capital burned in twenty or thirty places each night.

sentences.zh: 是歲四月，山東、河北大旱，至六月，雨複不止，民間斗米至千余錢。

translations.literal: That year, fourth month: Shandong and Hebei suffered great drought; by the sixth month rain would not stop, and in the markets a dou of grain reached more than a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year, fourth month, Shandong and Hebei suffered severe drought; by the sixth month rain would not cease, and grain in the markets reached more than a thousand cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 三年二月乙亥夜，大風從西北來，髮屋折木，吹清夷門關折。

translations.literal: Year 3, second month, on yihai night: a great wind came from the northwest, tore off roofs and snapped trees, and blew Qingyi Gate's bar broken.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, on yihai night, a great wind from the northwest stripped roofs, snapped trees, and broke Qingyi Gate's bar.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，大悲閣災，延燒萬餘家，火五日不絕。

translations.literal: Third month, on wuwu: Great Compassion Pavilion caught fire; the blaze spread through more than ten thousand households and the fire did not die for five days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu, fire took Great Compassion Pavilion and spread through more than ten thousand households; the flames burned five days without end.

sentences.zh: 山東、河北、河東諸路大旱。

translations.literal: Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong circuits suffered great drought.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong circuits suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 是歲，有男子郝贊詣省言：「上即位之後，天變屢見，火焚萬家，風折門關，非小異也，宜退位讓有德。

translations.literal: That year a man named Hao Zan came to the Secretariat and said: 「Since Your Majesty took the throne, heaven's warnings have come again and again — fire burned ten thousand homes, wind broke a gate bar; these are no small portents. You ought to abdicate in favor of one who has virtue.」
translations.idiomatic: That year a man named Hao Zan came to the Secretariat and said: 「Since Your Majesty ascended the throne heaven's warnings have piled up — fire consumed ten thousand homes, wind broke a gate bar; these are no trifling signs. You should abdicate to one of virtue.」

sentences.zh: 」有司問：「爾狂疾乎？

translations.literal: The responsible offices asked: 「Are you mad?」
translations.idiomatic: The offices asked: 「Are you mad?」

sentences.zh: 」贊大言曰：「我不狂疾，但為社稷計，宰相皆非其才。

translations.literal: Zan spoke loudly: 「I am not mad — I speak only for the altars of state; the chancellors are none of them fit for their posts.」
translations.idiomatic: Zan cried out: 「I am not mad — I speak for the realm; not one chancellor is fit for his post.」

sentences.zh: 」每日省前大呼，凡半月。

translations.literal: Each day he shouted before the Secretariat; this went on half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he shouted before the Secretariat; this lasted half a month.

sentences.zh: 上怒，誅之隱處。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and had him executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had him put to death in secret.

sentences.zh: 崇慶元年七月辛未未時，有風從東來，吹帛一段高數十丈，宛轉如龍，墜於拱辰門內。

translations.literal: Chongqing year 1, seventh month, at the wei hour before noon: wind came from the east and blew a length of silk dozens of zhang high; it twisted like a dragon and fell inside Gongchen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing 1, seventh month, at the wei hour before noon: wind from the east lifted a bolt of silk dozens of zhang high, coiled it like a dragon, and dropped it inside Gongchen Gate.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河東、陝西、南京諸路旱。

translations.literal: That year Hedong, Shaanxi, and Southern Capital circuits suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hedong, Shaanxi, and the Southern Capital circuit suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，放進士榜，有狂僧公言：「殺天子。

translations.literal: Year 2, second month: when the jinshi list was released, a mad monk cried aloud: 「Kill the Son of Heaven!」
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, second month, when the jinshi list was posted, a mad monk shouted: 「Kill the Son of Heaven!」

sentences.zh: 」求之不知所在。

translations.literal: A search was made but he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: They searched for him but could not find where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河東、陝西大旱，京兆斗米至八千錢。

translations.literal: That year Hedong and Shaanxi suffered great drought; in Jingzhao a dou of grain reached eight thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hedong and Shaanxi suffered severe drought; in Jingzhao a dou of grain cost eight thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐元年八月戊子夜，將曙，大霧蒼黑，跂步無所見，至辰巳間始散。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, Zhenyou year 1, eighth month, on wuzi night, just before dawn: a great fog, dark and green-black; one could not see a step ahead; it did not lift until between the chen and si hours.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, Zhenyou 1, eighth month, on wuzi night just before dawn: a dense fog, green-black; a man could not see his next step; it did not clear until the chen and si hours.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yimao, rain and tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, there was rain and tree ice.

sentences.zh: 時衛州有童謠曰：「團鸑冬，劈半年。

translations.literal: At the time in Weizhou there was a children's rhyme that ran: 「Round zuan winter, split half a year.
translations.idiomatic: About then in Weizhou children sang: 「Round zuan winter—half a year split apart.

sentences.zh: 寒食節，沒人煙。

translations.literal: Cold Food Festival, no human smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food Festival—no smoke of human habitation.

sentences.zh: 」明年正月，元兵破衛，遂丘墟矣。

translations.literal: 」The next year's first month, Yuan troops broke Weizhou, and it became a mound of ruins.
translations.idiomatic: 」The following first month Yuan forces stormed Weizhou, and the city was left a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，潮白河溢，漂古北口鐵裹關門至老王穀。

translations.literal: Second year, sixth month, the Chaobai River overflowed, sweeping from Old Northern Pass Iron-Wrapped Barrier Gate to Old King's Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, sixth month, the Chaobai River burst its banks and washed from Old Northern Pass Iron-Wrapped Barrier Gate to Old King's Valley.

sentences.zh: 庚申，南京寶鎮閣災。

translations.literal: On gengshen, fire at Southern Capital Baozhen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen fire broke out at Baozhen Pavilion in the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，上次宜村，有黃龍見於西北。

translations.literal: On renxu, the emperor encamped at Yicun; a yellow dragon appeared in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the emperor was at Yicun when a yellow dragon was seen in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 冬，黃河自陝州界至衛州八柳樹，清十餘日，纖鱗皆見。

translations.literal: Winter, the Yellow River from Shaanzhou border to Weizhou Eight Willows cleared for more than ten days; fine fish scales were all visible.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yellow River from the Shaanzhou frontier to Eight Willows at Weizhou ran clear for over ten days, every fine scale visible.

sentences.zh: 十二月己酉，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jiyou, rain and tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiyou, there was rain and tree ice.

sentences.zh: 三年二月戊午，大風，隆德殿鴟尾壞。

translations.literal: Third year, second month, on wuwu, great wind; Longde Hall ridge-beast finial damaged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on wuwu of the second month, a great wind wrecked the ridge-beast finial of Longde Hall.

sentences.zh: 三月戊辰，大風，霾。

translations.literal: Third month, on wuchen, great wind and dusty haze.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, a great wind blew with dusty haze.

sentences.zh: 四月，自去冬不雨，至於是月。

translations.literal: Fourth month, from last winter no rain until this month.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month it had not rained since the previous winter.

sentences.zh: 五月，河南大蝗。

translations.literal: Fifth month, great locusts in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Henan suffered a great locust plague.

sentences.zh: 六月，京城中夜妄相驚逐狼，月余方息。

translations.literal: Sixth month, in the capital at night people falsely panicked one another chasing wolves; only after more than a month did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the capital nightly erupted in false alarms as people chased supposed wolves; the uproar lasted more than a month.

sentences.zh: 十月丙申，西北有霧氣如積土，至二更乃散。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on bingchen, in the northwest mist like piled earth; it scattered only at the second watch.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, on bingchen: northwestern mist piled like earthen ramparts and did not lift until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 四年正月己未旦，黑霧四塞，巳時乃散，是春，河朔人相食。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, at jiwei dawn black mist closed on all four sides; it scattered at si hour; that spring people north of the river ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, first month, at jiwei dawn black mist walled the horizon and cleared only at si hour; that spring people in Hebei resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 五月，河南、陝西大蝗。

translations.literal: Fifth month, great locusts in Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Henan and Shaanxi were overrun by locusts.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔、扶風、歧山、郿縣騑蟲傷麥。

translations.literal: In Fengxiang, Fufeng, Qishan, and Mei counties fei insects damaged the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, Fufeng, Qishan, and Mei, fei insects ravaged the wheat.

sentences.zh: 七月，旱。

translations.literal: Seventh month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，飛蝗過京師。

translations.literal: On guichou, flying locusts passed over the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou clouds of locusts flew over the capital.

sentences.zh: 興定元年三月，宮中有蝗。

translations.literal: Xingding year 1, third month, locusts in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xingding 1, third month: locusts appeared within the palace.

sentences.zh: 四月，單州雹傷稼。

translations.literal: Fourth month, hail at Dan Prefecture damaged the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month hail in Dan Prefecture destroyed the crops.

sentences.zh: 陳州商水縣進瑞麥，一莖四穗。

translations.literal: Shangshui County, Chen Prefecture, presented auspicious wheat—one stalk, four ears.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshui County in Chen Prefecture presented auspicious wheat with one stalk bearing four ears.

sentences.zh: 開封府進瑞麥，一莖三穗、二莖四穗。

translations.literal: Kaifeng prefecture presented auspicious wheat—one stalk with three ears, two stalks with four ears.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng prefecture presented auspicious wheat: one stalk with three ears and two stalks with four ears each.

sentences.zh: 五月乙丑，河南大風，吹府門署以去。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on yichou, great wind in Henan blew the prefectural gate offices away.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on yichou: a great wind in Henan tore the prefectural gate offices from their places.

sentences.zh: 延州原武縣雹傷稼。

translations.literal: Hail at Yuanwu County, Yan Prefecture damaged the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Hail at Yuanwu in Yan Prefecture destroyed the crops.

sentences.zh: 七月癸卯，大社壇產嘉禾，一莖十五穗。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on guimao, auspicious grain appeared at the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain—one stalk with fifteen ears.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, on guimao: auspicious grain sprang up at the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain, one stalk with fifteen ears.

sentences.zh: 秋，霖雨。

translations.literal: Autumn, prolonged rain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn brought unending rain.

sentences.zh: 十月，邠州進白兔。

translations.literal: Tenth month, Bin Prefecture presented a white hare.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Bin Prefecture presented a white hare.

sentences.zh: 丹州進嘉禾。

translations.literal: Dan Prefecture presented auspicious grain.
translations.idiomatic: Dan Prefecture presented auspicious grain.

sentences.zh: 異畝同穎。

translations.literal: Different stalks sharing one ear.
translations.idiomatic: Different stalks shared a single ear.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，河南諸郡蝗。

translations.literal: Second year, fourth month, locusts in the prefectures of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, fourth month: locusts struck the Henan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五月，秦、陝狼害人。

translations.literal: Fifth month, wolves in Qin and Shaanxi killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month wolves in Qin and Shaanxi killed people.

sentences.zh: 六月，旱。

translations.literal: Sixth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 是歲，京師屢火，遣禮部尚書楊雲翼鋋之。

translations.literal: That year the capital repeatedly caught fire; Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi was sent to perform the halberd-clash rite against it.
translations.idiomatic: That year fires broke out again and again in the capital; Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi was dispatched to perform the halberd-clash rite.

sentences.zh: 三年春，吏部火。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, fire at the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, spring: the Ministry of Personnel burned.

sentences.zh: 四月癸未，陝右黑風晝起，有聲如雷，頃之地大震，平涼、鎮戎、德順尤甚，廬舍傾，壓死者以萬計，雜畜倍之。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on guiwei, a black wind rose by day in western Shaanxi with a sound like thunder; presently the earth quaked greatly; Pingliang, Zhenrong, and Deshun were worst hit—dwellings collapsed and those crushed to death numbered in the tens of thousands, with livestock losses twice that.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, on guiwei: a black wind rose in broad daylight across western Shaanxi, roaring like thunder, then the earth heaved; Pingliang, Zhenrong, and Deshun suffered worst—buildings toppled and the dead ran into the tens of thousands, with livestock losses double that count.

sentences.zh: 夏，旱。

translations.literal: Summer, drought.
translations.idiomatic: That summer brought drought.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬申，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on renshen, rain and tree ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, there was rain and tree ice.

sentences.zh: 四年正月戊辰二更，天鳴有聲。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, at wuchen second watch, the sky sounded with a voice.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, first month, at the second watch on wuchen the sky gave forth a sounding voice.

sentences.zh: 壬子，晝晦，有頃大雷風雨。

translations.literal: On renzi, noon went dark; soon great thunder, wind, and rain.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi noon turned dark as night; thunder, wind, and rain followed.

sentences.zh: 四月丁丑，大風吹河南府署飛百余步，戶案門鑰開，文牘飄散，不知所在。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on dingchou, a great wind blew the Henan prefectural offices more than a hundred paces; doors, desks, and locks flew open and documents scattered, their whereabouts unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, on dingchou: a gale hurled the Henan prefectural compound a hundred paces, burst doors and document chests, and scattered papers beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 六月，旱。

translations.literal: Sixth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 七月，河南大水，唐、鄧尤甚。

translations.literal: Seventh month, great flood in Henan; Tang and Deng suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Henan flooded; Tang and Deng were hardest hit.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，火。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on guiyou, fire.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on guiyou: fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，華州渭南縣民裴德寧家伐樹，破其中有赤色「太」字，表裏吻合。

translations.literal: That year, when Pei Dening of Weinan County, Huazhou, felled a tree at home, he broke it open and found within a red character 「太」, matching inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: That year Pei Dening of Weinan in Huazhou cut a tree on his property, split it open, and found a red 「太」 character within, identical inside and out.

sentences.zh: 有司言與唐大曆中成都瑞木有文「天下太平」者，其事頗同，蓋太平之兆也。

translations.literal: The authorities said it resembled the Tang Dali-era auspicious tree at Chengdu bearing the characters 「天下太平」; the matter was quite the same—probably an omen of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Officials said it recalled the Tang Dali auspicious tree at Chengdu inscribed 「All under Heaven at peace」—much the same sign, likely a portent of great peace.

sentences.zh: 乞付史館。

translations.literal: They requested it be handed to the Historiographical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the record be sent to the Historiographical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，以久旱，詔中外，仍命有司祈禱。

translations.literal: Fifth year, third month, because of prolonged drought, an edict went to court and countryside, and responsible offices were still ordered to pray.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, third month: after long drought an edict went throughout the realm and officials were again ordered to conduct prayers.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬寅，京師相國寺火。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renyin, fire at Xiangguo Temple in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on renyin: Xiangguo Temple in the capital burned.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁丑，霜附木。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on dingchou, frost adhered to trees.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on dingchou: rime frost clung to the trees.

sentences.zh: 先是，有童謠雲：「青山轉，轉山青。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a children's rhyme that ran: 「Green mountains turn, turn the mountains green.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand children had sung: 「Green mountains turn—turn the mountains green.

sentences.zh: 耽誤盡，少年人。

translations.literal: All delay exhausted, young men.
translations.idiomatic: Every delay spent, the young men gone.

sentences.zh: 」蓋言是時人皆為兵，轉鬥山谷，戰伐不休，當至老也。

translations.literal: 」It meant that then everyone became a soldier, turning and fighting through mountain valleys, warfare unceasing—they would reach old age in it.
translations.idiomatic: 」Men read it as saying that everyone had become a soldier, wheeling through mountain passes in endless war until youth itself was consumed.

sentences.zh: 元光元年四月，京畿旱。

translations.literal: Yuanguang year 1, fourth month, drought in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguang 1, fourth month: drought struck the capital region.

sentences.zh: 十月，上獵近郊，獲白兔，群臣以為瑞。

translations.literal: Tenth month, the emperor hunted near the suburbs and caught a white hare; the ministers took it as auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: on a suburban hunt the emperor took a white hare, and the ministers hailed it as a lucky sign.

sentences.zh: 明日，禦便殿，置鈴于項，將縱之，兔驚躍不已，忽斃幾上。

translations.literal: The next day, at the Informal Hall, a bell was hung on its neck and it was to be released; the hare leaped in fright without cease and suddenly died on the table.
translations.idiomatic: Next day at the Informal Hall a bell was tied about its neck for release, but the hare panicked and bounded until it dropped dead on the dais.

sentences.zh: 二年正月辛酉日午，有鶴千余翔於殿庭，移刻乃去。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, at wuwu noon, more than a thousand cranes soared over the palace courtyard and departed only after a quarter-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, first month, at wuwu noon a thousand cranes wheeled above the palace court and did not leave for a full quarter-hour.

sentences.zh: 七月乙卯，丹鳳門壞，壓死者數人。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on yimao, Danfeng Gate collapsed; several people were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, on yimao: Danfeng Gate gave way and several people were killed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，開封有虎害人。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, a tiger in Kaifeng killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: a tiger at Kaifeng killed people.

sentences.zh: 是時屢有妖怪，二年之中，白日虎入鄭門，吏部及宮中有狐狼，鬼夜哭于輦路，烏鵲夜驚，飛鳴蔽天。

translations.literal: At the time strange things recurred; within two years a tiger entered Zheng Gate in broad daylight, foxes and wolves appeared in the Ministry of Personnel and within the palace, ghosts wept at night along the imperial roadway, and crows and magpies startled at night, their cries blotting the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Strange omens piled up: within two years a tiger walked through Zheng Gate in daylight; foxes and wolves haunted the Ministry of Personnel and the inner palace; ghosts wailed along the imperial road at night; crows and magpies exploded into flight until their clamor darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 十二月，宣宗崩。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Emperor Xuanzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Emperor Xuanzong died.

sentences.zh: 哀宗正大元年正月戊午，上初視朝，尊太后為仁聖宮皇太后，太元妃為慈聖宮皇太后。

translations.literal: Aizong, Zhengda year 1, first month, on wuwu, the emperor first held court; the empress dowager was honored as Empress Dowager of Rensheng Palace, the Grand Consort as Empress Dowager of Cisheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Aizong, Zhengda 1, first month, on wuwu: the emperor held his first audience, raising the empress dowager to Rensheng Palace and the Grand Consort to Cisheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，大風飄端門瓦，昏霾不見日，黃氣塞天，仁聖又夢乞丐萬數踵其後，心惡之，占者曰：「後為天下母，百姓貧窶，將誰訴焉？

translations.literal: That day a great wind blew the tiles of Duan Gate; dusty haze hid the sun; yellow vapor filled the sky; Rensheng also dreamed of tens of thousands of beggars treading at her heels and was revolted at heart; the diviner said: 「Later you will be mother to all under Heaven—when the people are destitute, to whom will they appeal?
translations.idiomatic: That day gale winds stripped Duan Gate's tiles, haze swallowed the sun, and yellow vapor choked the sky; Rensheng dreamed ten thousand beggars at her heels and shuddered; the diviner said: 「You are to become mother of the realm—when the people are penniless, whom will they beg?

sentences.zh: 」遂敕京城設粥與冰藥以應之，人以為壬辰、癸巳之兆。

translations.literal: 」An edict was therefore issued to set out gruel and cooling medicine in the capital to answer it; men took this as an omen of the renchen and guisi years.
translations.idiomatic: 」So the capital was ordered to distribute gruel and cooling draughts in response; people read it as foretelling the disasters of renchen and guisi.

sentences.zh: 又有人衣麻衣，望承天門大笑者三，大哭者三，有司拘而問之，其人曰：「我先笑者，笑許大天下將相無人。

translations.literal: Again, a man in hemp garments facing Chengtian Gate laughed three times and wept three times; the authorities seized and questioned him; the man said: 「My first laughter laughed that so vast an empire had not a single worthy minister or general.
translations.idiomatic: Another man in hemp stood before Chengtian Gate, laughed three times, then wept three times; officials seized and questioned him; he said: 「I laughed first because so great an empire lacked a single worthy minister or general.

sentences.zh: 後哭者，哀祖宗家國破蕩至此也。

translations.literal: My later weeping mourned that the ancestral house and state had been battered to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: I wept afterward for the ancestral house and realm ruined to this point.

sentences.zh: 」有司以為妖言，處之重典。

translations.literal: 」The authorities deemed it demonic speech and would punish it by the heavy statute.
translations.idiomatic: 」Officials called it sorcerous talk and sought the heaviest penalty.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近詔草澤之士並許直言，雖涉譏訕亦不治罪，況此人言亦有理。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 「A recent edict allows men of the wilds to speak plainly; even if it touches on ridicule there is no crime—how much more when this man's words have reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 「A recent edict lets commoners speak plainly; even mockery goes unpunished—how much more when his words hold truth.

sentences.zh: 止不應哭笑闕下耳。

translations.literal: Only he should not have laughed and wept below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Only he should not have laughed and wept beneath the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 」乃杖之。

translations.literal: 」He was beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was flogged with the staff.

sentences.zh: 二年正月甲申，有黃黑之昆。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, on jiashen, a yellow-black swarm appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, first month, on jiashen: a yellow-black insect swarm appeared.

sentences.zh: 四月，旱。

translations.literal: Fourth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month there was drought.

sentences.zh: 京畿大雨雹。

translations.literal: Great hail in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region was struck by great hail.

sentences.zh: 三年春，大寒。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, spring: bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，有火自吏部中出，大如斛，流行輾轉，人皆驚避，逾時而滅。

translations.literal: Third month, on yichou, fire issued from within the Ministry of Personnel, large as a grain measure, rolling and turning as it moved; everyone fled in alarm; after a time it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on yichou: fire burst from the Ministry of Personnel, as large as a grain measure, rolling along the ground; people scattered in terror until it died away.

sentences.zh: 四月，旱、蝗。

translations.literal: Fourth month, drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month brought drought and locusts.

sentences.zh: 六月，京東雨雹，蝗死。

translations.literal: Sixth month, hail in eastern capital; the locusts died.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: hail in the eastern capital and the locusts perished.

sentences.zh: 四年六月丙辰，地震。

translations.literal: Fourth year, sixth month, on bingchen, earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month, on bingchen: an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 八月癸亥，大風吹左掖門鴟尾墜，丹鳳門扉壞。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on guihai, a great wind blew the ridge-beast finial from the Left Flank Gate; Danfeng Gate panels were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on guihai: a gale tore the ridge-beast finial from the Left Flank Gate and shattered Danfeng Gate's doors.

sentences.zh: 是日，風、霜損禾皆盡。

translations.literal: That day wind and frost destroyed the grain entirely.
translations.idiomatic: That same day wind and frost laid the crops waste.

sentences.zh: 五年春，大寒。

translations.literal: Fifth year, spring, severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, spring: bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 二月，雷而雪。

translations.literal: Second month, thunder and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: thunder with snow.

sentences.zh: 木之華者皆敗。

translations.literal: Trees that had blossomed all failed.
translations.idiomatic: Every tree that had flowered was ruined.

sentences.zh: 四月，鄭州大雨雹，桑柘皆枯。

translations.literal: Fourth month, great hail at Zheng Prefecture; mulberry and ramie all withered.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: great hail at Zheng Prefecture withered every mulberry and ramie plant.

sentences.zh: 京畿旱。

translations.literal: Drought in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 八月，御座上聞若有言者曰：「不放舍則何？

translations.literal: Eighth month, upon the imperial seat a voice seemed to speak, saying: 「If you do not grant amnesty, then what?
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: on the imperial seat a voice seemed to say: 「If you will not grant amnesty, then what?

sentences.zh: 」索之不見。

translations.literal: 」A search found no one.
translations.idiomatic: 」A search found no one there.

sentences.zh: 七年十二月，新衛州北三里許，有影在沙上，如舊衛州城狀，寺塔宛然，數日乃滅。

translations.literal: Seventh year, twelfth month, about three li north of new Weizhou, a shadow on the sand resembled old Weizhou city; temple towers stood clear; after several days it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, twelfth month: three li north of new Weizhou a shadow on the sand took the shape of old Weizhou, temple towers plain as life, and faded only after several days.
